data_points.claim: On public ARC-AGI-1 it reaches 29.5% pass@2.

The paper says this operating point breaks the previously reported ARC-AGI-1 cost–accuracy Pareto frontier.

data_points.claim: Intermediate reasoning is not decoded into language; computation happens in a recurrent latent workspace.
As of 2026-09-04, BDH-CQ is #1 on Hugging Face papers/trending (772 upvotes, published 2026-08-10).
Qwen3.8-27B is the Hub likes30d leader (13,878 likes, 5.7M downloads) — the popularity chart the paper is punching through.

common_questions: How can 150 million parameters be interesting when Qwen 3.8 is 27B?
What is latent reasoning if it is not chain-of-thought?
Is 29.5% on ARC-AGI-1 actually good, or just cheap?
Did they train on the evaluation tasks?
Where do I read the paper?

misconceptions.myth: Bigger parameter counts are the only trending AI story this month.
misconceptions.reality: Hub likes30d is dominated by 20B+ weights, but papers/trending #1 is a 150M latent reasoner.

misconceptions.myth: Reasoning models have to dump a chain of thought you can read.
misconceptions.reality: BDH-CQ updates recurrent memory from demonstrations, then iterates in latent space and decodes only the answer.

misconceptions.myth: ARC-AGI progress only counts as giant pass rates.
misconceptions.reality: The paper's claim is a new cost–accuracy Pareto point ($0.0007/task at 29.5% pass@2), not a raw SOTA score race.

audience_insights.knowledge_level: Shorts audience knows 'parameters' and 'ChatGPT thinks in text'. They do not know ARC-AGI scoring or latent recurrent workspaces. One number + one contrast is the ceiling.
pain_points: Paper PDFs are unwatchable on mute
